name: TCS Toronto Waterfront Marathon
summary: The TCS Toronto Waterfront Marathon is held in mid-October and is a World Athletics Elite Label race. The course runs through the downtown core and along the waterfront. It is known as a fast race, and the course records are among the fastest on Canadian soil.
courseHighlights: Start in downtown Toronto (Yonge Street in 2025)
Queens Quay and Lake Shore Boulevard along the waterfront
Return along Queen Street and Eastern Avenue
Finish at Queen and Bay, by Nathan Phillips Square

paceStrategy.summary: The route follows the lake, so there are few turns and no big hills in the sources. Pace evenly and watch the wind off Lake Ontario.

segments.terrain: Downtown streets, then the start of the waterfront
segments.advice: Start in a crowded field and run a calm first 5 km; do not weave through runners.

segments.terrain: Waterfront roads on Queens Quay and Lake Shore Boulevard
segments.advice: Hold an even pace; use other runners to block the wind if it is windy.

segments.terrain: Return through the Beaches, Queen Street and Eastern Avenue to downtown
segments.advice: Keep your effort steady and save a final push for the last 2 km.

fuelingNotes: The race site says there are aid stations about every 3 km, with electrolyte drink and energy gels offered on the course. Take your own gels if you use a different brand.
tips: The 2025 start moved to Yonge Street because of construction; check the current course map before race day
The 2025 Yonge Street start was narrower than the old University Avenue start, so expect a crowded first mile
Read the official event guide and the race weekend page for kit pickup, bag check and start corrals
Dress for cool October weather and wind from Lake Ontario

faq.question: Is the Toronto Waterfront Marathon flat?
faq.answer: The route follows Lake Ontario and has a reputation as a fast, flat course. The official site does not publish an elevation number.

faq.question: When is the Toronto Waterfront Marathon held?
faq.answer: It is held in October, usually on the second or third Sunday.

faq.question: Where does the Toronto Waterfront Marathon finish?
faq.answer: It finishes at Queen and Bay in downtown Toronto, close to Nathan Phillips Square.
